title: How a Seatbelt Works in 60 Seconds 🚗🔒 #shorts
description:
A seatbelt lets you lean forward freely, yet locks in an instant when the car stops hard. A spring keeps the belt snug, a weighted pendulum or a spinning lever locks a toothed gear, a small gas charge can pull the belt tight in a crash, and a twisting bar lets a little belt back out to protect your chest. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#seatbelt #carsafety #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A seatbelt lets you lean forward freely, but *locks in an instant* when the car stops hard.

steps.label: Spool
steps.text: Inside the retractor, a *spiral spring* turns a spool to keep the belt *snug*.

steps.label: Pendulum
steps.text: On a hard stop, a *weighted pendulum* swings forward and pushes a pawl into a *toothed gear*.

steps.label: Clutch
steps.text: Yank the belt fast and a *spinning lever* flies out and *locks* the spool too.

steps.label: Pretensioner
steps.text: In a crash, a small *gas charge* drives a piston that *pulls the belt tight*.

steps.label: Load limiter
steps.text: Then a *twisting bar* lets a little belt back out, so it doesn't *crush your chest*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spring, pendulum, *lock*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
